absent: Grace-period start, detection, completion and expedited handling for normal RCU.
Callback queuing, invocation and barrier semantics for call_rcu, synchronize_rcu and related wait helpers.
Publication primitive rcu_assign_pointer and its ordering guarantees.
Full struct rcu_head layout and its use beyond init and post-queue probe.
Updater-side and grace-period logic for SRCU tiny and tree variants.
Scheduler, preemption, bottom-half, per-CPU and lock-dependency primitives referenced as stubs.
Configuration selection controlling which alt variant is active.
Error handling and recovery beyond build-time offset checks and lock-dependency warnings.

findings.text: RCU removal for nulls-terminated hash lists detaches the node from readers and marks its backward link with a debug poison value to detect later misuse.

Head insertion, tail append and node replacement publish the new linkage with RCU ordering and repair neighbour backward links when neighbours exist; append on an empty list behaves as head insertion and the init replacement clears the old backward link.
Fake node setup creates an isolated marker whose backward link refers to its own forward field and whose forward link denotes the nulls terminator.

Iteration helpers traverse a nulls list until its terminator and expose each node as its enclosing object under RCU protection with a compiler barrier; the safe form remains usable when the current element is removed during the walk.
RCU header guards use a single definition to make repeated inclusion harmless.
Guarded RCU annotation marks a reference as residing in RCU address space and subject to RCU guarding discipline.
Unsigned sequence comparisons tolerate counter wrap by ordering on half-range distance rather than direct magnitude.
Sequence layout reserves two low bits for state with the remaining bits for count; shift is two and mask selects the low two bits.
Grace sequence state pairs two unsigned long counters for normal and expedited progress.
Active polling helper reserves two old-state slots.
Read-side nesting depth query reports the current task counter where preemptible RCU exists and reports a constant zero where that support is compiled out.
Low-level read-side control pins the current context against preemption across the region and restores it on exit, with an optional strict-mode hook that is empty in the shown configuration.

Normal and bottom-half read-side regions require paired entry and exit, forbid blocking, diagnose idle misuse, and track lock dependency; the bottom-half form additionally suppresses soft interrupt handling across the region.

Scheduler read-side regions rely on preemption control with paired tracking and idle diagnosis; notrace forms omit tracing; dont-migrate forms additionally pin the task against migration when preemptible RCU is enabled.
Hurry callback request falls back to normal queuing in this configuration; old-state polling comparison is simple equality.

Tasks RCU quiescent reporting centres on a per-task holdout flag cleared on voluntary switch or explicit checkpoint when execution was not preempted; several configurations define all reporting helpers as empty.
Where tasks RCU lacks a separate implementation its queue and wait operations alias normal RCU and task exit hooks are empty.

System-request, interrupt-work, idle-entry and deferred-wakeup controls are empty fallbacks; offload reports unsupported while de-offload reports success; nocb lock-dependency warning is active in one configuration and empty in the other.
Periodic soft-interrupt quiescent reporting is throttled to about ten hertz and is inactive under fully preemptible realtime.
Callback head initialisation and destruction helpers are empty for heap and stack use in this configuration.
Callback head lifecycle starts from an invalid sentinel at init and moves to queued for a specific function; a post-queue probe confirms the expected function and warns on corruption.
Deferred reclaim tolerates null input; two-argument forms use an embedded head while one-argument forms queue without it; a nolock form serves contexts without locking.
Embedding the reclaim head beyond a small offset from the object start is rejected at build time.
Lock-dependency tracking for RCU acquisition and release is active with checking support and empty without it, covering both normal and try acquisition.
Read-lock held queries affirm presence when dependency checking is off, except the scheduler flavour which reflects whether the context is non-preemptible.
Fallback helpers report dependency debugging as disabled and the current CPU as online.
Context switching or sleeping inside a read-side region is forbidden and diagnosed when checking is active across normal, bottom-half and scheduler flavours; checks are empty otherwise.

Read-side assertions warn only when debugging is enabled and the CPU is watchable and online, verifying the expected flavour is held or preemption is disabled; without checking they degrade to static assumptions and watching reports true.
Sparse address-space validation is enforced with checking support and empty without it; unrcu helpers strip the RCU annotation to yield a plain kernel pointer for local use.

Core access and dereference primitives perform a single volatile load with annotation validation; checking forms warn when the supplied protection fails, protected forms require an external holding condition, and raw forms impose no checking.

Initialisation helpers annotate a plain value as an RCU pointer for static or dynamic setup; handoff is an identity ownership marker; replace publishes a new value while returning the previously protected one; access reads without dereference guarantees.
Flavour-specific dereference wrappers accept the matching read-side held condition automatically, with combined and raw variants covering any flavour or unconditional use under protection.
Ordering after lock acquisition is a full barrier on architectures requiring it and empty elsewhere.
Trace and sleepable RCU held queries consult dependency state when checking is enabled and affirm presence otherwise.
Tasks-trace read-side entry acquires the dedicated sleepable domain through a fast path with dependency tracking and optional ordering, and exit releases it symmetrically.
Tiny sleepable RCU keeps two nesting counters selected by a shared index that toggles; locking briefly pins preemption to bump the current counter and encodes the index as the returned handle.
Tree sleepable RCU fast acquisition increments the currently published generation counter on the local CPU with containment against critical-section leakage.
